text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx rate and request latency observed for Hosted API and Dedicated pools in us-west-2 (Oregon). Group: inference-hosting. Alert ID: INC-2026-03015.

Liam B: paging oncall (us-west-2), seeing a spike in 5xx from edge. Clients reporting timeouts.

Elena S: I'm on it. First glance — spikes correlate with a surge of errors from AWS EC2 control plane API (DescribeInstances/AttachVolume throttling) per our cloud-client logs.

Priya R: confirm impact: Hosted API latency p95 up from 90ms to ~650ms and 5xx rate from 0.3% to 4.7% for the last 8m. Dedicated pools show increased queueing and a few connection failures.

Marco C: I'm running the routing checks now. It looks like the gateway nodes in us-west-2 are timing out when calling the autoscaler controller (AWS API) -> leads to scaling delays and some request rejections.

Liam B: Can we enable fallback routing to us-west-1 for new requests and mark us-west-2 for degraded? How quick is DNS TTL?

Elena S: We can flip the smart-router policy. Two mitigation steps: 1) update routing weights to prefer us-west-1 (gradual 80/20 -> 100/0), 2) disable auto-scaling triggers that rely on EC2 Describe calls and scale manually for Dedicated pools. Doing (1) now.

Priya R: tagging customers: start prep for CS note. Which customers are currently pinned to us-west-2 Dedicated?

Jorge C-S: list coming from support DB. Major pinned accounts: AcmeHealth (dedicated pool a-dc-7), Shoply (hosted, region pinned), FinEx (dedicated). I'll DM the owners and open priority support threads.

Elena S: router policy change command:

```
# update routing weights via admin API
POST /admin/routing/policy
{ "region_weights": { "us-west-1": 0.8, "us-west-2": 0.2 }, "reason": "us-west-2 AWS control-plane API throttling" }
```

Elena S: executed. Initial traffic shift started at 1784506905. Observability: p95 latency for us-west-1 increasing but still <200ms. us-west-2 5xx rate dropping slightly but still elevated.

Incident Bot: :information_source: Status update scheduled every 5m. Next update 1784507200.

Marco C: manual scale for Dedicated pools in us-west-2 initiated. Commands:

```
# scale out dedicated pool a-dc-7 by 3 nodes
./infra-cli pools scale --pool a-dc-7 --add 3 --reason "control plane throttling fallback"
```

Marco C: scale accepted by infra. Expected nodes to register in 6-9m due to orchestration delays.

Liam B: contacting AWS TAC. Looks like EC2 API request latencies and 429s coincide with the wider regional service degradation thread. Any link?

Support Bot: Created AWS Support Case: 1234567891. Case severity: 1. Linked to RITM-2026-9876. Support engineer assigned.

Priya R: customer impact summary for external comms (draft):
- Affected region: us-west-2 only.
- Symptoms: increased latency and elevated 5xx rates on Hosted API; Dedicated pools in us-west-2 experienced delayed scaling and intermittent failures.
- Mitigation: We routed new traffic to us-west-1 and manually scaled affected dedicated pools.
- Customer action: Customers pinned to us-west-2 will see restored capacity as nodes finish booting; recommend failing over to another region if low-latency requirement.

Elena S: observed an additional error pattern in kube-controller logs: repeated `ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded` from AWS Describe* calls. This matches EC2 control plane throttling.

Liam B: Any risk of data plane inconsistency if we move traffic regionally? We preserve model versions and pins, but double-check storage access (S3 endpoints).

Marco C: storage access is global S3; we've already validated model artifacts are available in us-west-1 via our artifact CDN. No expected data loss.

Jorge C-S: messaging to pinned customers going out now. Template: short incident note, impact, actions taken, ETA for resolution.

Priya R: CS wants list of any customer requests for credits. We'll capture after the incident ends.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Automated check: router-swap observed 75% of new requests to us-west-1 within 3m.

Elena S: After routing change and manual scaling, 5xx rate across platform reduced from 4.7% to 1.2% in 12m. p95 latency trending down to ~180ms overall. Still monitoring for flapping.

Liam B: AWS case update?

Support Bot: AWS Support Case 1234567891: AWS reports elevated internal API throttling in us-west-2 due to control-plane event. They are working on mitigation. No ETA provided.

Priya R: Let's prepare an interim status for dashboard and customers: severity P2, non-global outage, mitigation in place, active support case with AWS.

Elena S: I'm going to revert the router to normal weights once us-west-2 metrics are stable for two consecutive 5m intervals. If flapping resumes, we'll leave route preference to us-west-1.

Marco C: leaving on-call note with details and commands run. Handing off to night oncall (Lina) at 1784508000. Lina: please monitor AWS case and our internal throttling metrics, and keep CS looped.

Liam B: thanks team. Quick post-incident TODOs: 1) add exponential backoff for Describe* calls in autoscaler to reduce likelihood of cascading failures, 2) add a region-fallback runbook, 3) identify customers pinned to single region and recommend multi-region options.

Jorge C-S: acknowledged, will coordinate CS comms and credits assessment.

Incident Bot: :page_facing_up: Incident INC-2026-03015 transitioning to "monitoring" state at 1784508059.

Lina (oncall): acked handoff. Monitoring steady. Will update if AWS provides ETA or if metrics regress.

Elena S: final note before handoff: logs to review for RCA - `autoscaler.log`, `router-policy-audit.log`, AWS support transcript.

Liam B: great work, team. Closing active paging.
